html:
A Dutch oil company founded in 1890 to drill for oil in north Sumatra, in the Dutch East Indies. In 1907 it joined with the British Shell company to form the Royal Dutch Shell group, one of the giants of the oil age.

Its roots lie with Aeilko Zijlker, a tobacco planter who found oil in Langkat in north Sumatra in the 1880s. The company won the right to call itself royal from King William III. Under Jean Baptiste Kessler and then Henri Deterding, it built a refinery in Sumatra and sold kerosene for lamps across Asia, in a price war with Standard Oil of the United States.

The Shell Transport and Trading Company of the London merchant Marcus Samuel had pioneered tankers through the Suez Canal. In 1907 the two firms combined, with Royal Dutch holding 60 percent. The group drilled from Sumatra and Borneo to Romania, Mexico and Venezuela, and later competed with the Anglo-Persian Oil Company in the Middle East. The two parent companies fully merged in 2005, and the group took the name Shell plc in 2022, based in London.
